summary: Cycle 3 adopted the FIX-ORI-RN-004-2 bounded-lifecycle driver and advanced the matrix further than any prior attempt, but one driver-seam interaction remains. Landed (464028e9, d4938bb3): the fixed uniwind driver restored from main (23afaf8f via 31af7d88 — every lifecycle await bounded, per-leg budgets, fail-fast pipeline tail, run-scoped heartbeats; typecheck and scoped biome green against it unchanged), plus two orchestration corrections per the fix's handoff facts: the backend owner is reaped via a dedicated dispose() at phase teardown — NOT inside stop(), because the driver's endpoint-loss legs legitimately stop-then-restart the same owner mid-leg (the first c3 matrix failed every android leg with 'backend owner did not relisten within 15s' until this was split), and spawnBackendOwner pre-clears stale ledger-owned listeners before spawning. Progress this cycle: with a fresh simulator reboot (the documented IME restore after many marathon runs), the c3b run's uniwind engine drove real provider traffic end to end — reject-phase legs reached actual 'An error occurred while generating the response' states observed on-screen, and the live phase completed all native legs and entered the web leg, whose stop-turn and backend stop/restart the heartbeats tracked step by step (web/drive/stop-turn-checked, backend/stop/start at 08:04:18, the owner executing stop→restart→stop faithfully per its status file). The run then stalled exactly there: after the web leg's endpoint-loss backend stop, the driver never issued the following restart (no restart command in the owner's command file, no further heartbeats for 30+ minutes) — past the fix's 120s backend bound and 840s web budget, with the orchestrator idle in kevent and no chromium/expo/adb children. This is the same web-leg stall class one layer deeper, now localized to the driver's caller-provided-backend (options.backend) stop path — the path FIX-ORI-RN-004-2's own reviewer matrix (3/3 with the driver's self-launched backend) did not exercise. All processes were reaped, ports cleared, and the partial evidence tree removed (only the cycle-1 proof.red remains); typecheck and the scoped biome command are green on the committed tree.

The handoff's manifest semantics (completed literally means 3 platforms; key on legs[].status) required no runner change — this task's matrix always passes all three platforms to each driver invocation.

The handoff's teardown-ownership rule was initially over-applied (owner reaped inside stop()) which broke the driver's mid-leg stop→restart cycle; corrected to a dispose()-at-phase-teardown split after the c3 android legs diagnosed it.

The first c3 matrix's ios live legs failed at the marker-visible assertion after a ~15-marathon-run day on the reserved simulator; a full simulator reboot (the ORI-RN-005-documented IME restore) preceded the second attempt, after which all native legs passed.

The uniwind web leg producing delayed 'completed' rather than 'aborted' records for stop turns needs no runner change — the web target's stop proof comes from the runner's own web-self session, not the driver's web leg.
